section_summary.extract_value: This section reports between-sex comparisons on Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) scores: no significant sex differences were found for mean age or self-esteem, but there were significant sex differences in mean BMI. An ANCOVA covarying participants' BMI found a significant effect of sex on BAS scores (men higher than women), indicating men had more positive body appreciation independent of BMI. The section does not specify sample size, participant demographics, BMI assessment method, or any Pearson correlations between BAS and BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: One-way analyses of variance showed no significant sex differences in the mean age [F(1, 299) = 0.99, p > .05]and self-esteem [F(1, 299) = 0.15, p > .05]. There were, however, significant sex differences in mean BMI [F(1, 299) = 24.66, p < .05]. We, therefore, conducted a one-way analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) on BAS scores to investigate possible sex differences, with participants' BMI covaried out. The results of the ANCOVA showed a significant effect of sex [F(1,(299) = 9.09, p < .05; Cohen's d = 0.26], suggesting that men have a more positive body appreciation than women, irrespective of individual differences in BMI.
